title: Factorial designs
dek: A factorial runs combinations of factors on purpose so you can estimate main effects and interactions with the same budget. One-factor-at-a-time cannot see the interaction.
story: NIST’s industrial designs start with 2^k factorials: each factor at two levels, all combinations. With two factors A,B you see A, B, and AB from four cells. One-factor-at-a-time (change A, then change B from a new baseline) aliases the interaction into the “main effects” you think you measured.

In a genomics wet lab: medium × temperature, drug × lineage background, extraction kit × sequencer. If the kit effect reverses on one sequencer, that is an interaction. Publishing two separate one-way t-tests will miss it or mislabel it.

Replication of the whole factorial, or a fraction when k is large, is how you get an error term. A single unreplicated 2^k can still estimate effects; it cannot estimate σ² without extra assumptions (sparsity, higher-order interactions as noise).
deepTitle: Contrasts, aliasing, and GLMs on a design
deep: Main-effect contrast for a two-level factor: average of Y at + minus average at −, over the other factors. Interaction contrast: half the difference of those simple effects. In a balanced 2^2 these are orthogonal — SEs share σ²/n_cell geometry.
Fractional factorials alias higher-order interactions with mains. That is a designed bet that some interactions are negligible. Write the alias structure; do not treat a 2^{k−p} as a full 2^k.

Analysis: OLS or a GLM with dummy/coding for factors, plus the products for interactions. Blocking and randomisation still apply: randomise run order, block by day. A designed X matrix does not make ε spherical if drift exists.

In observational genomics, “factorial” is sometimes used loosely for a cross-tab of lineage × HIV. That is not a designed factorial; interactions are still scientifically real, but identification is the causal plates, not NIST’s run table.

formulas.label: 2² cell means
formulas.note: Four means, three orthogonal contrasts plus a grand mean in the usual coding.

formulas.label: Interaction contrast (two-level)
formulas.note: Difference of simple effects of A at the two levels of B.

visual.caption: A 2×2 of schematic cell means. Left: additive (parallel simple effects). Right: interaction (simple effects disagree). One-factor-at-a-time would have walked only two edges of the square and missed the crossing.

example.title: Drug × medium on MIC
example.setup: Two drugs, two media, 6 replicates per cell, log MIC. Cell means: (drug1, medA) 1.0; (drug1, medB) 1.1; (drug2, medA) 1.2; (drug2, medB) 2.0.

steps.title: Simple effects of medium
steps.body: For drug1, medium shift +0.1. For drug2, +0.8. Interaction contrast 0.7 on the log scale — a big deal, not a nuisance.

steps.title: OFAT trap
steps.body: If you only compared media for drug1, you would have declared media equivalent and never seen drug2’s medium disaster.

steps.title: Model
steps.body: OLS on log MIC with drug, medium, product. LRT or F for the product term is the interaction test. Then look at the four means; a star on the product is not a sentence.

example.takeaway: Run the rectangle. Interactions are differences of simple effects, and they are often the scientific object.

check.prompt: One-factor-at-a-time designs are weak for interactions because:
choices: They typically do not observe all combinations, so they cannot estimate how a simple effect changes across the other factor
Interactions equal main effects by definition
check.answer: They typically do not observe all combinations, so they cannot estimate how a simple effect changes across the other factor
check.why: The 2² needs four corners. OFAT walks two edges.

whyWrong.NIST requires OFAT for biology: NIST argues against OFAT as a default.

check.prompt: Cell means 4, 7, 6, 10 for (A−B−),(A+B−),(A−B+),(A+B+). Interaction contrast (ȳA+|B+ − ȳA−|B+) − (ȳA+|B− − ȳA−|B−) equals:
check.why: Simple effect of A at B+: 10−6=4. At B−: 7−4=3. Difference 1.

check.prompt: On the factorial small-multiples, the interaction panel is the one where:
check.figureHint: Right panel’s A+ B+ bar is not a parallel shift.
choices: The A+ B+ cell fails to look like “A main plus B main,” i.e. the simple effects disagree
check.answer: The A+ B+ cell fails to look like “A main plus B main,” i.e. the simple effects disagree
check.why: That is the crossing / non-parallel picture, drawn as bars.
